_help: Look of the world: environment (tonemap, grading, SSAO, fog) and sky colours per time of day and realm. Colours are hex. Read by World.cs. 'toon' is the anime look applied to every mesh (Toon.cs).

genshin._help: Genshin-style shader on characters (Genshin.cs, assets/shaders/genshin_*.gdshader). enabled false = back to the plain toon look.
genshin._rampsHelp: Shadow colours, multiplied with the base colour: [deep shadow, shadow, saturated band at the shadow edge]; the lit side is white. Warm on skin, cool violet on cloth and hair; night ramps bluer. metalMin: materials less metallic than this get no metal bands or highlight (leather and cloth were glossy).

env._help: tonemapMode: 0 linear, 1 reinhard, 2 filmic, 3 aces, 4 agx. ACES with lower exposure and stronger contrast and saturation: deeper, cleaner colours (Filmic looked flatter in tests). A strong sun over low ambient gives the clear lit/shadow split of the Genshin look; little haze keeps distant colours clean.
env._farFogHelp: A-05 (pale band where the view distance ends). farFog: the fog is at least this thick at the camera far plane (density = farFog / far plane metres; far plane = view distance + 200), so the ground is mostly fog-coloured where the far plane cuts it off. 1.2 changes nothing at the default 1200 m view distance (0.00086 is under fogDay) and only thickens the fog at short view distances; 0 = off.
env._sunHelp: Sun colour at noon, while low (morning/evening) and at dusk; ambient = the sky fill light in shadow. Warm sun over a cool, dim fill gives the real-daylight look.
env._nightHelp: Night is a light dusty purple (the owner's wish, 2026-11-27), never black: nightTop/nightHorizon colour the sky (lavender), ambientNightColor/ambientNight the fill light (mauve, strong enough to see by), moonColor/sunNight the lilac moonlight. Was dusty blue and much darker: nightTop 0a0e16, nightHorizon 262c38, ambientNightColor 4e5a72 at 0.7, moon 9fb2dc at 0.75.
env._qualityHelp: gi: bounce light on/off (SDFGI), giEnergy its strength; ssil: screen-space indirect light; volFog: haze density for sun shafts (0 = off), sunShafts their strength; shadowDistance: metres of sun shadows.
env._godraysHelp: Golden-hour light shafts (quality >= 2, reduced by rain): godrays 1/0 on/off, godraysDensity extra volumetric haze, godraysAniso forward scattering, godraysLength metres, godraysEnergy extra sun energy in fog, godraysMorning morning strength.

weather._help: Weather.cs: chances of the next state (rest is rain), seconds between changes (real time; a day lasts 720 s), fade seconds, rain streak and splash counts.

terrain._help: Ground textures (assets/textures/terrain, CC0 ambientCG) blended by World.cs TerrainShader. *_tile = metres per repeat; *_tint multiplies a texture; saturation/brightness grade the whole ground; meadow_amount = dirt patches in the grass; gravel_amount = gravel patches.
terrain._edgeHelp: A-05 (bright line along the edge of the block square, about 90 m out). The smooth far ground no longer stops exactly at the edge of the block square: it carries on vox_inset metres into the square, pushed vox_drop metres down, so it dives under the blocks (a block top can sit half a metre under the smooth ground, and the sky showed through that slit). vox_inset must be at least two terrain cells (1 m at home, 1.6 m on the other lands); vox_drop more than 0.5. Was: cut exactly at the edge, no drop (0 and 0).
terrain._setHelp: _set = folder under assets/textures with the six ground layers: 'terrain' (ambientCG photos) or 'terrain_painted' (the painted anime pack, tools/kit_gen/tex_gen.py). The block named after the set overrides the values above while that set is in use.

sky._belowHelp: A-05: the sky under the horizon (seen where the far plane cuts the ground and the sea off). It is the fog colour mixed belowSkyMix toward the horizon colour (the colour fogged far ground has; was the horizon colour darkened 55%), reached at belowRate x the slope under the horizon (40 = fully there 1.4 degrees down; was 5 = 11 degrees, which left a bright band).

water._seaHelp: A-05: seaDrawY = height the far sea plane is drawn at. -0.12 is the surface of the block sea (water blocks fill to y 0, a source's top is 0.88 of its block), so the two meet level at the edge of the block square. Was 0.25 (the sea level used for swimming and shores, unchanged), which left a 0.37 m step with the pale sea bed showing through it.
